bibliographic.title: Fostering effective hybrid human-LLM reasoning and decision making
bibliographic.authors: Passerini, A., Gema, A., Minervini, P., Sayin, B., & Tentori, K.
bibliographic.citation_apa: Passerini, A., Gema, A., Minervini, P., Sayin, B., & Tentori, K. (2025). Fostering effective hybrid human-LLM reasoning and decision making. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, 7, 1464690. https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2024.1464690

methodology.method_family: perspective article; narrative argument and literature-informed discussion
methodology.technology_context: Large Language Models (LLMs), chatGPT, human-AI hybrid collaboration, question-answering, text generation, Natural Language Processing

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed perspective on human-LLM collaboration, biases, mutual understanding, and complementary team performance. Provided text supports relevance to human oversight and LLM risk themes, but does not substantively address conversational governance mechanisms, regulated high-stakes deployment, audit, compliance, observability, or operational controls. Best classified as foundational contextual framing rather than central governance evidence.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial PDF text was supplied; later sections may contain additional governance, oversight, or domain-specific content not visible in the excerpt.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal reflects a conceptual perspective article, not an empirical study. Several CASP/JBI-style criteria are not applicable due to absence of primary data collection in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The perspective presents a coherent argument for prioritizing human-LLM interaction research and cites known LLM limitations, but the supplied excerpt offers limited direct evidence on conversational governance in regulated settings and no empirical evaluation of governance interventions.

coding.theme: Hybrid human-LLM reasoning and decision making
coding.subtheme: Biases, mutual understanding, and complementary performance in human-LLM teams

synthesis.main_claim: Future LLM research should prioritize effective human-LLM interaction by addressing collaboration biases and pursuing mutual understanding and complementary team performance in reasoning and decision making.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a conceptual research agenda for hybrid human-LLM collaboration, highlighting underexplored collaboration risks and pointing toward bias mitigation and hallucination management as part of effective teaming.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text does not describe empirical validation, regulated-domain deployment, or operational governance mechanisms such as audit, compliance, logging, or conversational control frameworks.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence for human oversight, hybrid intelligence, and collaboration-risk framing; not as primary evidence for conversational governance implementation in regulated environments.
